1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a ring oscillator configured to generate a plurality of independent first entropy values;
a countermeasure circuit configured to detect and mitigate phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator;
one or more logic circuits operatively coupled to the ring oscillator and countermeasure circuit, the one or more logic circuits including:
a first processing stage that receives the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator and applies at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
a second processing stage that seeds a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
a third processing stage that generates a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
a fourth processing stage that produces a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the fourth processing stage is configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the fourth processing stage is configured to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the countermeasure circuit includes at least one of: a jitter injection module, a frequency modulation module, or a phase randomization module configured to introduce variations that prevent phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator.

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators, and the first processing stage is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent ring oscillators.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the first processing stage is configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single ring oscillator.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the first processing stage is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the first processing stage is configured to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the first processing stage is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the first processing stage is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the first processing stage is configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the first processing stage is configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
generating a plurality of independent first entropy values from a ring oscillator;
detecting and mitigating phase tracking attacks on the ring oscillator using a countermeasure circuit;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes at least:
implementing a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator is a single ring oscillator, and wherein generating the plurality of independent first entropy values includes generating the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single ring oscillator.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the ring oscillator comprises a plurality of independent ring oscillators, and wherein generating the plurality of independent first entropy values includes generating the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent ring oscillators.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein detecting and mitigating phase tracking attacks includes introducing at least one of: jitter injection, frequency modulation, or phase randomization to the ring oscillator.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.
